analysis.title: Multi-Asset Strategy Daily
key_insights: 10Y UST yield is around 4.91% after briefly trading through 4.90% in Friday's risk-off move. Brent gapped lower toward $110 a barrel, partly from the contract roll and partly on renewed hopes for diplomacy with Iran after a new Axios report.
Trump has said discussions with Iran, with Qatari mediators, have been productive and that no new US strikes will take place before tomorrow's midterms.
Mizuho expects the AI complex to remain an important cross-asset driver after Friday's tech sell-off. Equities recovered overnight.
Today tests whether the duration bid has further to run. Mizuho economists see room for a small downside surprise in ISM manufacturing, and the Treasury borrowing estimates kick off a refunding week.

A Democratic sweep in the midterms is increasingly the market's base case. Mizuho thinks positioning should stay cautious into the result, with tighter regulation of the AI sector one possible consequence. The outcome for rates is less clear.

Mizuho would stay cautious about chasing the duration rally. Softer ISM, oil and risk sentiment can keep the 10Y below 5% for now, but the Treasury refunding estimates (QRA), politics and Friday's payrolls leave event risk.

The 10Y Bund yield is in the low 3.30s after reaching 3.363% on Friday. Bunds should follow oil and USTs today. German gas storage is about 62% entering winter, well below the 80% target, which leaves European rates exposed to another energy shock.

France should stay under pressure after Fitch changed its outlook to negative from stable and kept the A+ rating, citing weaker growth, higher borrowing costs and a wider deficit. OATs widened about 10bp versus Bunds on Friday and Mizuho sees little reason to fade the move yet.

Mizuho expects the BoE to hike 25bp to 4.00% on Thursday (7-2 vote split), then another 25bp in Q1-27. That is a much less aggressive path than the market, which prices 100bp+ over the next year. Mizuho prefers receiving GBP rates relative to other DM markets, particularly the US.
Asian equities rose on lower oil despite Chinese manufacturing and non-manufacturing PMIs both below 50. JGBs bear-steepened into the ultra-long end ahead of the US midterms.
